title: Contact and Asset
premise: Beatrix Oyelaran, a private security contractor who has spent years erasing himself from every database, is guarding a nervous tech executive on a transatlantic flight when the aircraft's records vanish mid-flight—erased by the same shadowy firm that once employed him. Hunted by his former handlers and pursued by a federal investigator who suspects he's complicit, Beatrix must decide whether to trade the one secret worth killing for: proof of a sanctioned assassination disguised as an accident, implicating people at the highest levels. As allies die and his polished lie unravels, he chooses loyalty to truth over survival, leaking the evidence through a journalist while sacrificing his own anonymity—and nearly his life—to bring justice outside the law.
about_author: Casper Fairweather is the pen name of a former aviation logistics consultant who spent a decade inside the gray zone between corporations and governments before walking away. He writes thrillers about people whose jobs require them to be forgettable, drawing on a life spent in airport lounges and safe houses across four continents.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag Rule
chapters.summary: Beatrix Oyelaran's POV. In Lagos, Beatrix preps for a routine protection detail: pack light, stay unmemorable, keep the go-bag by the door. We learn his rules for invisibility and the polished lie of his identity. Emotional beat: controlled calm masking a man who trusts no one, including himself.

chapters.title: Client Nobody Trusts
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. His new client, tech executive Adaeze Nwosu, hires him for a flight to Geneva, paying triple rate in cash and refusing to explain why she's terrified. Beatrix notices she's being followed but takes the job anyway—the money funds his next disappearance. Beat: greed wrestling with instinct.

chapters.title: Wheels Up
chapters.summary: Adaeze's POV. Aboard the private jet, Adaeze reveals fragments: her company's encryption was used to move something that shouldn't exist. She carries a drive she won't surrender. Beatrix pretends not to care. Beat: two liars circling each other at 40,000 feet.

chapters.title: Vanishing Point
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Mid-Atlantic, every trace of the flight evaporates—transponder logs, manifests, air traffic records. The jet lands at a strip that officially has no flights scheduled. Beatrix recognizes the signature: Meridian Group, his old employers. Beat: cold dread as his past finds him.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Investigator Dana Reyes' POV. Reyes, a federal auditor chasing financial ghosts, notices the impossible: a flight that carried passengers but never existed. She pulls Beatrix's file and finds a man made of contradictions. Beat: the hunter enters the story, sharp and skeptical.

chapters.title: Old Handlers
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. In Geneva, Beatrix's former Meridian handler, Sable, offers him a clean exit if he delivers Adaeze and the drive. Beatrix stalls, buying time while memorizing exits. Beat: the sick familiarity of dealing with people who own your history.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Adaeze's POV. Hiding in a Meridian-linked safehouse Adaeze booked under a dead aunt's name, she and Beatrix finally compare notes. Her drive contains flight telemetry proving a passenger jet was downed deliberately—a sanctioned hit dressed as mechanical failure. Beat: reluctant alliance forged in fear.

chapters.title: Reyes Closes In
chapters.summary: Reyes' POV. Reyes traces the vanished flight's insurance payout to a shell company with Meridian fingerprints. Her supervisor warns her off; she escalates instead. She interviews Beatrix, who lies beautifully—but she clocks the lie. Beat: cat-and-mouse tension, mutual recognition of competence.

chapters.title: What the Drive Holds
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Decoding the telemetry, Beatrix finds his own name in the operational chain—he was unknowingly part of the cover-up's logistics years ago. The secret worth killing for is also his indictment. Beat: guilt detonating quietly beneath professional composure.

chapters.title: Sable's Patience Ends
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable reports to Meridian's directorate that Beatrix has seen too much. Orders come down: retrieve the drive, leave no witnesses. Sable requests one exception—Beatrix alive—for reasons even Sable doesn't fully admit. Beat: menace with a flicker of something almost human.

chapters.title: Geneva, After Midnight
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A Meridian snatch team hits the safehouse. Beatrix and Adaeze escape through service tunnels, but Adaeze is grazed and the backup drive is taken. They realize the original is hidden where only Adaeze can reach it. Beat: adrenaline, loss, deepening dependence.

chapters.title: The Journalist Option
chapters.summary: Adaeze's POV. Adaeze proposes going public through investigative journalist Tomas Lindqvist, whom she half-trusts. Beatrix argues leaks get people killed; Adaeze argues silence already has. They split the evidence as insurance. Beat: ideology clashing—loyalty versus truth made explicit.

chapters.title: Reyes Goes Rogue
chapters.summary: Reyes' POV. Stripped of the case by orders from above, Reyes copies her files and keeps working off-book. She finds Beatrix again—not to arrest him, but because he's the only thread left. An uneasy truce forms. Beat: justice outside the law begins here.

chapters.title: Lindqvist's Price
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Meeting Lindqvist in Copenhagen, Beatrix learns the journalist needs verification from a second source—Meridian insider archives in Zurich. Lindqvist warns that publishing paints a target on everyone involved. Beatrix volunteers himself. Beat: the moment hiding stops being an option.

chapters.title: Zurich Vault
chapters.summary: Beatrix and Adaeze's alternating POV. Inside Meridian's Zurich archive, they photograph corroboration—until Sable appears, alone, and lets them walk out. 'I owed you one,' Sable says, though Beatrix can't place the debt. Beat: betrayal of one's own side, mercy as mystery.

chapters.title: The Debt Explained
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Flashback woven into present: years ago Beatrix, without knowing it, refused an order that would have killed Sable's sister on that same 'accident' flight pattern. Sable's loyalty was bought long ago. Beat: the theme inverted—loyalty to a person over loyalty to power.

chapters.title: Everything Burns
chapters.summary: Reyes' POV. Meridian burns its paper trail: Lindqvist's office is torched, Adaeze's company lawyers vanish, and Reyes is framed for leaking classified files. She goes fully underground and contacts Beatrix with one sentence: 'They're coming tonight.' Beat: the walls closing in from all sides.

chapters.title: Trade the Secret
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Cornered, Beatrix makes the trade: he offers Meridian a fake drive location to draw their leadership to one intercept point, while feeding the real evidence to three news outlets simultaneously. Reyes provides the legal teeth; Adaeze provides access. Beat: gambit, terror, resolve.

chapters.title: Intercept
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The trap springs at a decommissioned airfield. Meridian's retrieval team walks into Reyes' federal colleagues and live cameras. Sable arrives anyway, gun drawn, and chooses not to fire—instead handing Beatrix the directorate's internal ledger. Beat: climax, violence held at the last inch.

chapters.title: Fallout
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The story breaks globally: resignations, arrests, a Senate inquiry. Adaeze testifies and rebuilds her company on honest terms. Reyes is reinstated with a promotion she doesn't trust. Meridian's directors scatter to jurisdictions without extradition. Beat: victory with ash in its mouth.

chapters.title: The Price of Truth
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Justice came, but Beatrix is now the most identifiable man in his profession—his invisibility spent like currency. Sable disappears without goodbye. Beatrix buries the old lie and, for the first time, unpacks the go-bag. Beat: grief and strange relief intertwined.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, epilogue. Six months later, a stranger slides Beatrix a note in a Lisbon café: someone else's records have just vanished mid-flight. He looks at the packed bag by his feet, then leaves it there and follows the stranger out. Beat: quiet hope—he'll fight in the open now, and the story turns one more page.
